Subject: Weekend retrain: request for latency variance carveout and amendment

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the partnership. Quick background: HexaHealth runs a weekly model retrain every Saturday 02:00–06:00 PT that reindexes a large portion of our embeddings and triggers a burst of re-ingestion and long-context scoring. During the retrain window we observe a short-term spike in tail latency (p90–p99) for our dedicated pool. Our product team is asking whether Redwood can provide an official carveout in the Dedicated SLA for scheduled maintenance-driven latency variance.

What we need: an explicit exception that allows up to 99.5th percentile latency to degrade to 220–300ms (current SLA target is 50ms p99 for our reserved GPUs) for up to 4 hours/week during a customer-notified maintenance window. We understand the need to balance fairness for other tenants; we are open to a narrow, contractual carveout (defined window + notice + observability weave).

Attached: retrain_schedule.csv (times & dataset sizes) and SLA_requirements.pdf (internal asks).

Can Redwood confirm process and whether you’d accept a time-boxed amendment or temporary variance for our Dedicated pool? If so, please outline what telemetry you’d require and any expected cost delta. We’re aiming to finalize this as an amendment to our reserved capacity contract (deal attached on our side).

Best,
Sarah Wu
Head of ML Ops, HexaHealth

Thanks Sarah — helpful context and the attachments came through. We’re glad you raised this early. High level: Redwood is open to defined, scheduled carveouts for retrain events, provided there are clear boundaries (window, notice, and telemetry).

Quick clarifying Qs before we scope the amendment:
- Is the Saturday 02:00–06:00 PT window fixed, or do you expect occasional shifts/monthly changes?
- During the retrain, what fraction of traffic is mission-critical (latency-sensitive) vs. background batch scoring? Any sample traces would help.
- Do you want the SLA change to apply to only the reserved pool serving production inference, or both production + staging tenants hosted on the same reservation?

I’ve attached an initial draft (proposed_carveout_draft.docx) that sketches amendment language and two options: (A) limited latency variance with no extra cost but a stricter notice & telemetry obligation, (B) guaranteed extra headroom (dedicated burst nodes) for the window at an uplifted monthly fee.

Ben — can you pls add recommended telemetry and an ops playbook we’d require for the first 30 days of the amendment? Lauren — I’ll loop you into procurement once we align on option.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync later today? I have availability 14:00–15:30 PT.

Hi all — technical note from the SRE side (longer but wanted to be explicit):

Summary: We can support a scheduled, narrow latency variance carveout for customer-managed retrains with two supported approaches. Each has trade-offs on cost, isolation, and operational complexity.

Option 1 — Time-boxed SLA variance (no extra nodes):
- Amendment language: allow p99 to exceed baseline up to X ms for up to 4 hours/week during customer-scheduled windows. Redwood will not issue credits for performance inside that window provided the customer ships notice >=48 hours and provides retrain/runtime manifest.
- Telemetry required: per-request latencies (p50/p90/p99), token counts, concurrency histogram, and a short-lived trace sample for slow requests (one trace per minute during the window).
- Operational expectations: HexaHealth must set a maintenance flag via API to enable KV cache warm-up and expected batch/priority routing. We will monitor and provide a post-window report.
- Pros/Cons: cheapest for customer but risk of cross-tenant tail if background jobs spike.

Option 2 — Bounded burst headroom (reserved burst nodes):
- Amendment language: Redwood provisions N additional reserved GPUs (burst pool) attached to your dedicated allocation during the retrain window. These nodes are billed as a scheduled burst uplift.
- Telemetry: same as Option 1 + node-level GPU utilization and per-node queue depth.
- Pros/Cons: predictable tail behavior, stronger SLA; higher cost.

Suggested SLA phrasing (draft): "For customer-scheduled maintenance windows (notified >=48 hours), Redwood will not apply SLA credits for latency exceedances occurring within the approved maintenance windows up to 4 hours/week. If customer elects Scheduled Burst Headroom, Redwood will provision the agreed burst capacity and maintain p99 latency under 100ms for production workloads while the burst pool is online."

Cost: rough order of magnitude — Option 1: no immediate cost increase; Option 2: uplift ~15–30% of monthly reserved capacity price depending on size of burst pool. We’ll produce a precise uplift once you confirm target QPS and model sizes.

Next steps: 1) confirm whether HexaHealth wants Option 1 or 2; 2) provide QPS/trace samples for a representative week; 3) we’ll produce amendment wording + DocuSign-ready doc.

Note: we can also pilot Option 2 for two scheduled weekends to validate end-to-end behavior before committing to billing changes.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions/SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
